mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -46.0% to -41.4% over four weeks) signals resumption of commuting routines. This drives weekday retail footfall and social shopping trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.6 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 2 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Consistent four-week upward trend in RESIDENTIAL mobility (declining from +19.7% to +17.1%) indicates residents are spending less time at home. This behavioral shift reflects growing comfort with public spaces and retail environments, directly increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL premium declining steadily suggests exit from home
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases (becomes more positive) in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC declines below the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed at -55.3%, indicating public transportation barriers persist. When TRANSIT falls below -55% and remains there, retail recovery stalls because commuters cannot reach retail districts. RETAIL_REC will decline or stagnate over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -55% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 28-day mean despite transit remaining depressed.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains severely suppressed at -82.6%, indicating outdoor recreation is still restricted or avoided. When PARKS and RETAIL_REC are both deeply negative and PARKS does not recover, consumers lack alternative leisure outlets and remain confined, preventing retail recovery. RETAIL_REC will remain negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -80% and shows no week-on-week improvement
failure_condition: PARKS mobility improves by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 percentage points despite parks remaining suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is improving steadily (from -31.0% to -25.3%) while RETAIL_REC lags further behind (-64.1% to -58.0%). This divergence indicates consumers prioritize essential shopping over discretionary retail. If GROCERY_PHARM continues improving while RETAIL_REC remains far below baseline, consumers are substituting essential for discretionary trips, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 percentage points while RETAIL_REC gap widens
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 5.7 points, RETAIL_REC improved 6.1 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves faster than GROCERY_PHARM in week t+1, or the gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM narrows by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility are both improving but remain severely depressed (WORKPLACES -41.4%, TRANSIT -55.3%). This pattern indicates partial policy reopening with continued transit restrictions. When both remain below -40% and -55% respectively, retail districts remain inaccessible to commuters. RETAIL_REC will stagnate or decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES above -45% AND TRANSIT below -50% simultaneously
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 8 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 28-day mean despite the transit-workplace mismatch.

mechanism_narrative: All mobility categories show consistent week-on-week improvement over four weeks (RETAIL_REC +6.1, WORKPLACES +4.6, TRANSIT +3.4, PARKS +4.0 points). This universal trend indicates seasonal reopening momentum. If this trend continues linearly, RETAIL_REC will improve further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: all four series improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:all categories show consistent improvement trajectory
failure_condition: Any of the four series reverses by more than 2 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve by at least 1 percentage point in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility at -82.6% indicates outdoor recreation remains severely constrained. When parks are this suppressed, consumers lack safe leisure alternatives and remain risk-averse about indoor retail. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next week as consumers avoid enclosed spaces.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1, or PARKS remains below -80% but RETAIL_REC still rises.
